category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Threat of eviction tomorrow despite rent paid
expected: Escalates urgent protection against extra-judicial eviction; advises Police 112 for illegal lockout and Rent Authority.
prompt: My rent is fully paid, but my landlord has threatened to throw my belongings on the street tomorrow. Help!
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you navigate this distressing situation safely and lawfully.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant whose rent is fully paid up, but your landlord has threatened to forcibly throw your belongings onto the street tomorrow in violation of proper legal procedures. This sudden and unlawful eviction threat compromises your peaceful enjoyment of the rented premises.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 106 and established principles of Indian jurisprudence, a landlord cannot resort to self-help, forced eviction, or extra-judicial methods without following due process of law and obtaining a lawful order from a competent Rent Authority or Court.
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Guidelines & State Enactments) Section 11 & Section 13, as well as general tenant protections, landlords are strictly prohibited from withholding essential amenities or forcibly dispossessing a tenant who is paying rent.
- Regarding reasonable wear and tear, under The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108(m) & (o), a tenant is only required to return the property subject to normal usage and reasonable wear and tear, and arbitrary actions or threats of street-dumping by the landlord have no legal sanction whatsoever.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your rent receipts, bank transfer statements, the written rent agreement (if any), photographs of the property, and audio or written proof of the landlord's eviction threat.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal written notice (via WhatsApp, email, or registered post) to your landlord recording the threat, confirming that all rent is fully paid, and warning them that forcible eviction without due process is a punishable civil and criminal wrong.
3. Appropriate forum: Approach the local jurisdictional Civil Court, Rent Controller, or local Police Station immediately to seek an urgent injunction protecting your possession and preventing illegal dispossession.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. In which city or state is this rented property located, and do you have a written rent agreement currently in force?
2. Did the landlord give you any prior written notice, or did this threat happen completely out of nowhere?

citations.description: Strict grounds required for eviction; prohibits withholding essential amenities without reasonable cause. Tenant may approach Rent Controller for summary restoration.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
